title: Sabha: Indraprastha
hook: Narada adds a warning to Pandu's request and leaves; everyone says yes, and Yudhishthira sends for Krishna
carry: send for the one who sees further

segments.voice: Yesterday: Pandu's words, carried by Narada, asking his son to perform the Rajasuya. Your line was tell my son.

Narada has one more thing to say before he goes. This sacrifice, he tells the king, is hard to finish. It has many obstacles. Brahma-rakshasas, demons who haunt sacrifices, look for any flaw in it. And after it, a war can come that destroys the warriors of the earth. Think it over, Narada says. Do what's good for you. Then he leaves, and the hall is left holding both halves of the message.
screen: `HARD TO FINISH.` → `DEMONS LOOK FOR FLAWS.` → `A WAR CAN COME AFTER.`

segments.voice: A dead father asking his son to rise to this. A sage warning that it might end in ruin. Yudhishthira brushes aside neither. The text says he sighed, and thought, and couldn't find peace. So he does what a king in a sabha is supposed to do: he asks. First his ministers and his brothers. They all say the same thing: you deserve this, the time is right, do it. Then the priests and sages around him, Dhaumya, and Vyasa himself. They agree too. Everyone in the room says yes. And still Yudhishthira doesn't move. The text gives his reasoning. People who love you don't always point out the danger. Some say what pleases. Some are carried along by their own hopes. So he thinks of one person who sees further, who won't flatter him, and who knows the world: Krishna. He sends a fast messenger to Dwaraka, and Krishna comes quickly to Indraprastha. A unanimous yes doesn't end his asking. He isn't looking for a no. He's looking for someone who will tell him the truth, either way. A sabha is a room full of counsel, and the best use of it is knowing whose counsel you most need. This is the last day of the hall's own story. Everything from here leans toward the sacrifice. Tomorrow, Krishna answers.
screen: `A REQUEST AND A WARNING.` · `EVERYONE SAYS YES.` · `LOVE DOESN'T ALWAYS SEE DANGER.` · `SEND FOR THE ONE WHO SEES FURTHER.` · then, large: `A UNANIMOUS YES IS NOT AN ANSWER.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a decision in front of you, large or small, and notice who has already told you yes. Then ask yourself quietly who would tell you the truth about it, even if it isn't what you want to hear. Let a face come; you don't have to call them, just know who it is, and breathe with that.
Sabha. A hall full of counsel. Today, every voice in it says yes, and the king still sends for one more.
Your line: send for the one who sees further. Everyone said yes, and he still asked once more. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Hindu tradition remembers Krishna in the Mahabharata as a counselor as well as a god, and his advice to the Pandavas is often retold alongside the story of the Rajasuya.

chat.says: Everyone told Yudhishthira yes. Why did he still send for Krishna?
options: Friends don't always name the danger, so he wanted someone who'd tell the truth.
He needed Krishna's army, since his own brothers had refused to fight.
Narada had told him to ask Krishna before doing anything at all.
chat.meaning: Yudhishthira reasoned that those who love you may only say what pleases. So he sent for Krishna, who sees further and won't flatter.

Brahma-rakshasas.meaning: demons said to haunt sacrifices, hunting for flaws

Dwaraka.meaning: Krishna's city, where the messenger is sent

Krishna.meaning: the Pandavas' cousin and counselor, honored as God

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Sabha Parva, Lokapala Sabhakhyana Parva (Narada's warning) and Rajasuyarambha Parva (Yudhishthira consults ministers, brothers, Dhaumya and Vyasa, and sends for Krishna)

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm Narada's warning: many obstacles, Brahma-rakshasas seeking flaws, and a war destroying kshatriyas after the sacrifice.
Confirm Yudhishthira consults ministers and brothers, then Dhaumya and Dvaipayana (Vyasa), who all approve.
Confirm Yudhishthira's reasoning that friends may not point out faults out of affection or self-interest before he sends for Krishna.
Confirm Krishna is sent for at Dwaraka (Dwaravati) and comes quickly.
